problemStatement.formal: RH := ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 ∧ 0 < s.re ∧ s.re < 1 → s.re = 1/2. The same proposition is already defined twice in the gallery — in proofs/Proofs/RiemannHypothesis.lean (def RiemannHypothesis, line 128, via isNonTrivialZero) and in proofs/Proofs/PrimeNumberTheoremOQ01.lean (def RiemannHypothesis, line 69) — but no theorem currently bridges them.
problemStatement.plain: Riemann Hypothesis (Millennium Prize, 2000): every non-trivial zero of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) lies on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2. This slug was seeker-extracted from the parent prime-number-theorem-oq-01 and largely duplicates the existing 'riemann-hypothesis' gallery slug (status COMPLETED, 41 axioms in proofs/Proofs/RiemannHypothesis.lean). Any meaningful S(N) work on this slug must target a narrow tractable adjacent result, NOT the open conjecture itself.

proven: ζ has no zeros for Re(s) > 1 (Mathlib: riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re).
Functional equation ζ(s) ↔ ζ(1-s) via completedRiemannZeta_one_sub.
PNT itself (Hadamard / de la Vallée-Poussin 1896) — formalised in Proofs/PrimeNumberTheorem.lean as PrimeNumberTheorem_Ratio / _Equiv / _Error / _Li with the analytic core axiomatised.
Hardy 1914 (infinitely many zeros on the critical line) — axiomatised in RiemannHypothesis.lean as hardy_infinitely_many_on_critical_line.
Robin (1984), Mertens-Littlewood (1912), von Koch (1901) equivalent reformulations — axiomatised as RH_iff_Robin / RH_iff_Mertens / RH_iff_PrimeCounting in RiemannHypothesis.lean.
open: RH itself — open since 1859; Millennium Prize Problem since 2000. Not tractable in any formalisation session.
Easier direction of RH ↔ Mertens (RH → M(x) = O(x^{1/2+ε})) — blocked on Mathlib lacking the Riemann-von Mangoldt explicit formula for ψ(x).
Easier direction of RH ↔ von Koch / prime counting — same Mathlib gap.
Robin's equivalence (RH ↔ σ(n) < e^γ·n·log log n for n > 5040) — blocked on Mathlib lacking colossally-abundant-number / Gronwall infrastructure.

insights: S4 (researcher-3, 2026-05-14): A v4.26.0 silent-regression pattern surfaced on `Proofs/PrimeNumberTheoremOQ01.lean` (parent slug `prime-number-theorem-oq-01`, 10 days stale on origin/main). The pattern is **missing transitive import of Nonvanishing.lean** — at v4.26.0, the canonical zeta-non-vanishing lemmas (`riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, `riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`) were extracted from a deep-imports module and now require **explicit** import of `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Nonvanishing` (which transitively imports Dirichlet). Any RH/PNT-adjacent proof file importing only the lightweight `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta` will surface this regression on first v4.26.0 Docker baseline. Detection heuristic: grep for `riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_l[et]_re` in any `Proofs/*.lean` file that imports `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta` but NOT `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Nonvanishing`; if a hit appears, that file has the regression.

mathlibGaps: No formal Riemann-von Mangoldt explicit formula ψ(x) = x − ∑_ρ x^ρ/ρ + ... (blocks RH ↔ Mertens, RH ↔ prime counting easy directions).
No formal Mertens-function bound infrastructure beyond ArithmeticFunction.moebius (blocks Mertens-conjecture-style reformulations).
No formal logarithmic integral Li(x) as a Mathlib primitive (defined locally in PrimeNumberTheoremOQ01.lean as a placeholder).
No formal Robin-class / colossally-abundant-number / Gronwall API (blocks RH ↔ Robin discharge).
No formal Riemann–Siegel formula or Backlund / Hardy–Littlewood zero-counting bounds.
